item.title: Club hurling glory for Ballygunner
item.description: The All Ireland Club Hurling final has been won by Ballygunner. The Waterford kingpins beat Galway's Loughrea 1-20 to 1-14 at Croke Park It's their first title since 2022 and their second overall while the wait for a first ever All Ireland goes on for Loughrea. Advertisement Hurling's Kehoe Cup final was won by Wicklow who defeated Meath by 16 points to 3-6.

item.title: Ireland midfielder scores on Liverpool debut
item.description: Denise O'Sullivan scored 7 minutes into her Liverpool debut in the Women's FA Cup today. The Cork woman made the move from North Carolina Courage last night and was instantly slotted into the team. The Republic of Ireland midfielder played 72 minutes for the Reds who ran out 6-0 winners over the London Bees 6-0 in their 4th round tie Advertisement There were also wins today for Manchester City, Manchester United and Tottenham.

item.title: British qualifier causes the first shock of Australian Open
item.description: British qualifier Arthur Fery caused the first shock of the Australian Open by beating Italian 20th seed Flavio Cobolli on day one. The world number 185 won in straight sets in Melbourne, matching the biggest victory of his career in his first overseas Grand Slam main draw. The world's top ranked players are both safely through - with Carlos Alcaraz and Aryna Sabalenka both winning. item.title: Newcastle held by Wolves
item.description: Newcastle have missed the chance to go fifth in the Premier League as they were held to a goalless draw at bottom side Wolves. The result ends a winning run of three top flight games for the visitors. Advertisement

item.title: Lidl National Football League round-up
item.description: The 2026 Lidl National Football League got under way on Sunday with four games in Division 4 of the competition. Carlow, relegated last year after winning the Division 4 title two seasons ago, got their campaign off to a winning start when they edged out Sligo by 1-7 to 1-4 at SETU Carlow. Carlow laid the foundation for victory in the opening half and a goal from Cliodhna Ní Shé helped them lead by 1-3 to 0-2 at the break. item.title: All-Ireland glory for Dingle
item.description: Dingle have won the most dramatic of AIB All Ireland Senior Club Football Championship finals. A point at the end of extra time from Mikey Geaney saw them defeat St.Brigids 0-23 to 1-19. Dingle trailed at half time by 9 points to 7. It was 0-17 1-14 at the end of regulation time. Advertisement Tom Rooney reports === Galway beat Mayo by 2 points in the FBD League final. Advertisement The Tribesmen got the better of their neighbours by 2-12 to 1-14 this afternoon.

item.title: Dingle win All-Ireland Senior Club Football Championship
item.description: Dingle are All-Ireland Senior Club Football Champions. The reigning County Football Champions overcame St Brigid's of Roscommon in extra time to win 0-23 to 1-19. Radio Kerry's Tim Moynihan and Ambrose O'Donovan were there for the winning point: Advertisement

item.title: Civic reception planned in Killarney to honour Jessie Buckley
item.description: Plans are in the works to hold a civic reception for Golden Globe winner Jessie Buckely in her native Killarney. The 36 year-old actress is tipped to be the first Irish woman to win an Oscar since Brenda Fricker for her role in Hamnet.
